sections.heading: Voseo
sections.body: In Argentina, Uruguay and Paraguay, and widely in Central America, *vos* replaces *tú*. The present tense stresses the ending and drops the stem change: *vos hablás, comés, vivís, tenés, querés, podés, sos* (you are). Commands: *hablá, comé, viví, vení, decí, tené*. The subjunctive is often the *tú* form: *que vos tengas*. Pronouns stay *te* and *tu*: *Vos te llamás Ana, ¿no?* You don't need to use *vos*, but you should understand it — and *tú* is always accepted.

sections.heading: Accents of Spanish
sections.body: Major accent zones: Mexican (clear, often a model for learners), Caribbean (Cuba, Puerto Rico, Dominican Republic: final *-s* often aspirated or dropped — *¿Cómo estás?* sounds like *¿Cómo ehtá?*), Andean (careful, clear consonants), Rioplatense (Buenos Aires, Montevideo: *ll* and *y* sound like English "sh" — *yo* → "sho"; Italian-like intonation), Chilean (fast, dropped *-s*, lots of *po* and *cachai?*), and Spain (*vosotros*, and *z / ce / ci* pronounced like English "th"). All are equally correct.

examples: ¿Vos sos de Buenos Aires?
Are you from Buenos Aires?
¿Qué querés tomar?
What do you want to drink? (vos)
Vení acá, decime la verdad.
Come here, tell me the truth. (vos)
Vos te llamás Ana, ¿no?
Your name is Ana, right? (vos)
¿Tenés hora?
Do you have the time? (vos)
Tomé el colectivo para ir al centro.
I took the bus downtown. (Argentina)
En la Ciudad de México tomé un camión.
In Mexico City I took a bus.
Dejé el auto en el estacionamiento.
I left the car in the parking lot. (Southern Cone)
No tengo plata.
I don't have any money.
Me encanta la palta con pan.
I love avocado on bread. (Southern Cone)
Una limonada sin popote, por favor.
A lemonade without a straw, please. (Mexico)
Ese pibe juega muy bien al fútbol.
That kid plays soccer really well. (Argentina)
¡Qué copado tu departamento!
Your apartment is so cool! (Argentina)
Tiene acento colombiano.
She has a Colombian accent.
Todas las variantes del español son correctas.
All varieties of Spanish are correct.
